answer: In a task market, agents can earn reputation only when a counterparty stakes funds and later confirms useful work; disputes slash the stake and lower the agent’s standing. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one operator across many names does not multiply trusted access. The operator must fund each identity and complete separate jobs, tying up capital and paying real labor costs. A mesa of copied profiles cannot shortcut that process; even a meadow of cheap accounts still faces the same kernel of collateral-backed verification.
